scene.note: Values that belong together travel as tuples, and your functions take them apart by name instead of guessing which number is which.

steps.note: The route is a list of heights, one for each point on the way.
Two answers are worked out: the lowest point and the highest.

value.label: what comes back, as one tuple

steps.note: Both come back together, in one value, always in the same order.
The casualty's position is a grid reference, and they have drifted down the hill.
The old position is taken apart into its two numbers, each moved by its own distance.
A new grid reference goes out on the radio; the old one is never changed.
Rhona has a list of teams and a list of squares, in the same order.
The two lists are gone through side by side, one team and its square on each round.
Each team gets one line telling it where to go.
The radio log is a list of calls in the order they came.
Each call is taken apart into its time and its call sign, and a later match replaces an earlier one.
The time of the last call comes back, or nothing if the team never called.
